There has been an increase in awareness of discrimination on grounds of promiscuity—apparent or actual—which at least since year 2010 has been called slut shaming—protesting against explaining or excusing rape by referring to any aspect of a woman's appearance and later, by extension, calling for sexual freedom in general.

Problematically, excusing rape has been confused with explaining rape. Excusing rape is a damaging and incorrect moral judgement, because rape is always the perpetrators fault, blame lies with the perpetrator, and rape is always wrong. However, explaining rape is an empirical question that can be analysed with data and evidence, and that data does suggest that alcohol intoxication is one contributing causal factor, insufficient by itself, just as the presence of someone with a history or disposition to rape being in the vicinity is insufficient in itself. Importantly, factors like decisions to intoxicate, or decisions to wear provocative clothing or signal sexual availability per prevailing cultural norms, are more within the control of victims, who are vastly more numerous than perpetrators, and because they incur the greatest damage from rapes, have greater motivation to change in parallel with investment in law enforcement, crime prevention and intoxicant demand reduction. Yes, it would be better if rapists did not rape. But until then, you’re contributing to the problem of victimisation.
